# MethodCache: instructions for coding agents

Copy this file into your project as agent instructions, for example as `.github/copilot-instructions.md`, a Cursor
rule, a Claude Code skill or a section of `AGENTS.md`. It tells a coding agent how to add caching with MethodCache
correctly. Full docs: https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/README.md

Bulk source reads are guarded against key, tag and clear invalidation; invalidated candidates are not published. Collection subclasses with public state are hashed with both that state and their elements. Static tags do not format arguments, and templates format only the parameters they reference.

## Adding caching to a service

1. The `MethodCache` package contains the library, the source generator and the analyzers. Nothing else is needed
   for in-memory caching. All packages require .NET 10 and the .NET 10 SDK.
2. Put `[Cache]` on the **interface** method, never on the class. Put `[CacheInvalidate(Tags = [...])]` on the
   interface methods that change the data. Don't change the implementation.
3. Register services as usual, then call `builder.Services.AddMethodCache()` **after** them. Later cacheable
   registrations fail at host startup or first generated binding. Missing services require explicit
   `AutoRegister(lifetime)` and exactly one accessible implementation in the selected generated module.
4. Use `MethodCacheBuilder` for startup, in one `AddMethodCache(mc => mc...)` call: `Defaults`, `Group`, typed
   `Method`, `Memory`, `Distributed`, `Telemetry`, `FromConfiguration`, `FromAssemblyOf<T>()` and the integrations'
   `UseRedis` / `UseSqlServer` (one of them) / `UseMessagePack`. Don't use `services.Configure<...>` for MethodCache
   options. Choose a module explicitly when multiple assemblies generate the same interface. Keep all add-on/Core
   versions identical.

```cs
using MethodCache;

public interface IProductService
{
    [Cache(Duration = "00:10:00", Tags = ["products", "product:{id}"])]
    Task<Product> GetAsync(int id, CancellationToken ct = default);

    [Cache(Duration = "00:01:00", Tags = ["products"])]
    Task<List<Product>> SearchAsync(string text, int page);

    [CacheInvalidate(Tags = ["products", "product:{id}"])]
    Task UpdateAsync(int id, Product product);
}

public sealed class ProductService(Database db) : IProductService
{
    public Task<Product> GetAsync(int id, CancellationToken ct = default) => db.LoadProductAsync(id, ct);

    public Task<List<Product>> SearchAsync(string text, int page) => db.SearchAsync(text, page);

    public Task UpdateAsync(int id, Product product) => db.SaveAsync(product);
}
```

```cs
builder.Services.AddSingleton<Database>();
builder.Services.AddScoped<IProductService, ProductService>();   // any lifetime
builder.Services.AddMethodCache();                               // after your registrations
```

## Rules

- Only interface methods that return a value can be cached: sync, `Task<T>` or `ValueTask<T>`. Return a list, never
  a lazy `IEnumerable<T>` or `IQueryable<T>`.
- Callers must use the interface. Calling the method from inside the class, or resolving the class itself, bypasses
  the cache.
- Keys are generated from the method and its arguments; don't write keys for `[Cache]` methods. A `CancellationToken`
  is not part of the key. Every value that changes the result must be a parameter.
- Tags take templates with a **parameter name** only: `"product:{id}"`. `"{product.Id}"` is not a template, stays
  literal and gives warning MC0016; add an `id` parameter instead. Use the same tags on the cached method and on its `[CacheInvalidate]`.
- Dynamic tag arguments use `MethodCacheKeys.Part` formatting: colons and backslashes in strings are escaped,
  null has its own marker, and numeric/date formatting is invariant. Use the same helper for manual invalidation.
  Tags share an application-defined namespace; different literal templates can still select the same tag. Prefer
  ids (`int`, `Guid`) and never pass passwords or tokens as arguments of cached methods.
- Durations accept invariant `[d.]hh:mm:ss` or unit strings such as `30s` and `1.5h`. Other settings: `SlidingExpiration` (or `"off"`), `RefreshAhead`
  (shorter than `Duration` and `SlidingExpiration`, or `"off"`; MC0023 otherwise), `FailSafe` (or `"off"`), `FailSafeTimeout`, `FailSafeRetryAfter`,
  `Version`, `Tags`, `Enabled`, `Distributed` and the named `Group` setting. In code each has one builder method with
  the same name: `WithFailSafe(d)`, `WithFailSafeTimeout(t)`, `WithFailSafeRetryAfter(t)` and so on.
- Cached objects are shared between callers: return immutable types such as records.
- For a type with only private state used as an argument or inside one (a property, a list element), implement
  `ICacheKeyProvider`.
- For library modules and Native AOT, select the containing assembly with `MethodCacheBuilder.FromAssemblyOf<T>()`.
  If multiple modules generate the same interface, select exactly one; calling/entry assemblies have no special priority.
- In `appsettings.json`, the `MethodCache` section holds `Defaults`, `FailSafe`, `Groups` (by group name) and
  `Methods` (by method id, such as `[MyApp]MyApp.IProductService.GetAsync`; not `Services`). Write durations as
  `"00:05:00"` (a bare number is rejected), `Tags` as a list, and only known setting names. Anything else, an
  unknown method id and a method listed twice fail startup.
- `CacheWhen` is set for one method in code (`mc.Method(...).CacheWhen(...)`); in `Defaults` or a group it fails
  startup.
- For a client from a NuGet package with an interface, use
  `[assembly: CacheInterface(typeof(IClient), nameof(IClient.Method), Duration = "...")]` instead of a wrapper.
- Without an attribute, use `ICacheManager.GetOrCreateAsync(key, factory, o => o.WithDuration(...))` with an explicit,
  prefixed key such as `$"order:{id}"`.
- Fix MethodCache's `MC` build diagnostics; each links to its explanation, and many have a code fix.
- In tests, register `NoOpCacheManager` (namespace `MethodCache`) after `AddMethodCache()` to turn method caching
  off. HTTP response storage remains independent; use its own options and administrator.
- To invalidate a `GetOrCreateAsync` entry that has a version, pass the key and the version:
  `InvalidateKeyAsync(key, version: 2)`. Never pass a stored key (`MethodCacheKeys.StoredKey`) to `ICacheManager`.
- To invalidate one call of a `[Cache]` method, get its key from `IMethodCacheKeys`:
  `cache.InvalidateKeyAsync(keys.For<IProductService>(s => s.GetAsync(42)))`. For every entry of one method, use
  `ICacheAdministrator.InvalidateMethodAsync(keys.MethodId<IProductService>(s => s.GetAsync(0)))`.
- Several registrations of one interface with different implementation types each cache their own results.
- Use `UseRedis` or `UseSqlServer`; owned storage never falls back to the app's `IDistributedCache`. Configure only `DistributedCacheOptions.KeyPrefix` before building the container; use a new container for connection/prefix changes.
- `AddHttpCaching()` requires explicit `AddMethodCache()` in the same container, in either order. HTTP uses a separate `MaxHttpBytes` budget (100 MiB), or exclusively the configured native MethodCache Redis/SQL transport. Never use the app cache as a fallback. Send explicit Cookie headers, or set `KeepCookies=true` to preserve transport cookies and bypass response caching. Confirmed unsafe mutations still advance shared URL epochs.

## Namespaces

- `MethodCache`: `[Cache]`, `[CacheInvalidate]`, `[CacheInterface]`, `ICacheManager`, `ICacheAdministrator`,
  `IRuntimeCacheConfigurator`, `IMethodCacheKeys`, `MethodCacheKeys`, `MethodCacheMemoryOptions`, `Any<T>`,
  `ICacheKeyProvider`.
- `MethodCache`: also `NoOpCacheManager` (sealed). Serializer, transport and atomic-store interfaces are internal.
- `Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection`: `AddMethodCache`. Everything else is a method on its builder:
  `FromConfiguration`, `Distributed(...)`, `Telemetry(...)`, `UseRedis` (package `MethodCache.Redis`), `UseSqlServer`
  (package `MethodCache.SqlServer`) and `UseMessagePack` (package `MethodCache.Serialization.MessagePack`).

SQL backplane gap discovery remains non-blocking even for long transactions: only a separate non-waiting probe retires old missing identities. HTTP selection-rule changes retire a URL epoch once, preserving newer concurrent publications even if deletion fails after rotation. Gap failure coverage runs without infrastructure in the Core fault-injection suite, with linked SQL integration checks for real locking semantics.

The public ICacheManager contract is GetOrCreateAsync (a state-passing factory, like HybridCache), TryGetAsync,
InvalidateKeysAsync and InvalidateTagsAsync, all with the caller token last. CacheEntryOptions is immutable. Custom managers store
entries under MethodCacheKeys.StoredKey(key, version) and use CanCache; generated calls pass keys that already carry their
version, with Version = null, and generated synchronous calls bypass a custom manager. Runtime configurators expose only
UpsertAsync/RemoveAsync/ClearAsync (ValueTask) and GetOverrides(). They reject unknown method ids and retire local policy generations. Declarative L2 namespaces are stable; runtime behavior
changes use private random namespaces. Never reintroduce cache callbacks, a factory context object, public policy pipelines,
key generators or backplanes. Recovery has independent L2 and publication counters and bounded queues.

Use named attribute settings (`Group = "name"`); `CacheKeyAttribute` and raw keys are unsupported. Omitted flags inherit, explicit false overrides. Duration grammar is shared by configuration and attributes (`30s`, `1.5h`, `[d.]hh:mm:ss`); ordinary durations must be positive. Turn an inherited sliding expiration, refresh-ahead or fail-safe off with `"off"` in attributes/configuration or `TimeSpan.Zero` in the builder. Format dynamic tag arguments with the canonical key-part rules; do not interpolate culture-dependent values manually.

Select JSON with `UseJson(context)` for Native AOT or `UseJson(options)` for explicit settings. Options are owned snapshots. `VerifyRoundTrip` defaults to true but does not prove nested polymorphic/private data preservation. SQL schema changes require explicit migration; do not use automatic DDL to reinterpret existing unversioned tables. Entry format/serializer versions change value namespaces; logical tombstones, wire-v1 invalidations and HTTP epochs remain format-independent.

Core owns container-scoped `IMeterFactory` instruments and its `MethodCache` ActivitySource. The OpenTelemetry package
only provides AddMethodCacheInstrumentation builder subscriptions. Never add metrics-provider interfaces, manager
wrappers or baggage propagators. Core MethodCacheTelemetryOptions controls explicit key/tag span opt-ins; hashes are
the default when keys are enabled. No keys/tags/URLs/user/tenant metric dimensions, copied HTTP attributes or exception
payloads in spans/logs. Preserve application ambient activity/baggage context. Attributes are namespaced
(`methodcache.kind`, `methodcache.method`, `methodcache.result` and so on). Histograms use seconds. Report local
method/HTTP entries, HTTP bytes, observed L2 entries and TotalWeight in configured units, never object-memory estimates.
Health checks honor failureStatus and independently report L2, backplane subscription and storage/publication queues.

- Generated keys and method ids start with the service assembly simple name in brackets, without its version. Closed generic argument identities include their assemblies. Never write a key or method id by hand: get keys from `IMethodCacheKeys.For` and ids from `IMethodCacheKeys.MethodId`, administration, or typed configuration expressions.

<!-- source: docs/getting-started.md -->

# Getting started

MethodCache 1.0 is a release candidate on nuget.org, so add `--prerelease` until 1.0.0 is out (the same goes for
the add-on packages):

```bash
dotnet add package MethodCache --prerelease
```

The `MethodCache` package contains the library, the source generator and the analyzers. It requires .NET 10 and the .NET 10 SDK. The same minimum applies to every add-on package.

## 1. Start from a service

A typical service talks to a database on every call:

```cs
public sealed class ProductService(Database db)
{
    public Task<Product> GetAsync(int id, CancellationToken ct = default) => db.LoadProductAsync(id, ct);

    public Task<List<Product>> SearchAsync(string text, int page) => db.SearchAsync(text, page);

    public Task UpdateAsync(int id, Product product) => db.SaveAsync(product);
}
```

## 2. Put the attributes on its interface

`[Cache]` goes on interface methods that return data, `[CacheInvalidate]` on the methods that change it. The class
only gains `: IProductService`; its methods don't change:

```cs
using MethodCache;

public interface IProductService
{
    [Cache(Duration = "00:10:00", Tags = ["products", "product:{id}"])]
    Task<Product> GetAsync(int id, CancellationToken ct = default);

    [Cache(Duration = "00:01:00", Tags = ["products"])]
    Task<List<Product>> SearchAsync(string text, int page);

    [CacheInvalidate(Tags = ["products", "product:{id}"])]
    Task UpdateAsync(int id, Product product);
}

public sealed class ProductService(Database db) : IProductService
{
    public Task<Product> GetAsync(int id, CancellationToken ct = default) => db.LoadProductAsync(id, ct);

    public Task<List<Product>> SearchAsync(string text, int page) => db.SearchAsync(text, page);

    public Task UpdateAsync(int id, Product product) => db.SaveAsync(product);
}
```

- `GetAsync(42)` is stored for ten minutes under a key built from the method and its argument
  (`...IProductService.GetAsync:42`). The `CancellationToken` is not part of the key.
- `"product:{id}"` is a tag template: `GetAsync(42)` is tagged `product:42`.
- `UpdateAsync(42, ...)` removes every entry tagged `products` or `product:42` once it has completed.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> The attributes must be on the interface. On a class they do nothing, and the analyzer reports
> [MC0001](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/user-guide/DIAGNOSTICS.md#mc0001) with a code fix that moves them.

## 3. Register it

```cs
builder.Services.AddSingleton<Database>();
builder.Services.AddScoped<IProductService, ProductService>();   // any lifetime
builder.Services.AddMethodCache();                               // after your registrations
```

`AddMethodCache()` wraps every registered interface that has cached methods in its generated decorator and keeps the
lifetime you chose. Register cacheable services before this call. A later cacheable registration fails at host
startup, or when a generated decorator first binds without a host. Unrelated services may be registered later.
Calling `AddMethodCache` again decorates newly added services and keeps existing decorators intact.

Missing implementations are registered only with explicit `AutoRegister(ServiceLifetime.Scoped)` (or another
lifetime). Select the generated module with `FromAssemblyOf<ProductService>()`; exactly one accessible concrete
implementation must exist for each missing service. Zero or multiple candidates give an error naming the service,
module and candidates. Explicit DI registrations always retain their implementation and lifetime.

When multiple assemblies generate decorators for the same interface, select one module with
`FromAssemblyOf<SomeTypeInThatAssembly>()`. No entry-assembly or alphabetical preference is applied. The same
module selection and candidate data work under JIT and Native AOT.

Keyed registrations (`AddKeyedScoped<IProductService, ProductService>("primary")`) are cached too, under the same
key; an interface registered only keyed is not also registered without a key. The service key is part of the cache
keys, so each keyed registration of an interface caches its own results; it must be a string, enum, bool, char,
integer or `Guid` ([Keys](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/keys.md#things-to-know)). A catch-all registration with `KeyedService.AnyKey` is
rejected, since its implementation is created for whichever key is requested; register concrete keys instead.
A constructor parameter marked `[ServiceKey]` receives your key, as without MethodCache.

Several registrations of one interface, such as `AddScoped<IPriceProvider, StorePrices>()` and
`AddScoped<IPriceProvider, PartnerPrices>()` resolved as `IEnumerable<IPriceProvider>`, each cache their own results;
the implementation type is part of their keys. Two registrations of the same implementation type share their results
([Keys](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/keys.md#things-to-know)).
Open generic registrations and closed types without a generated binding also give a named startup error.

Generic interfaces work the same way: `IRepository<User>` is cached for every closed type a class in your project
implements, such as `UserRepository : IRepository<User>`. An open generic registration such as
`AddScoped(typeof(IRepository<>), typeof(Repository<>))` gives a named binding error at startup or first binding
without a host; register generated closed types instead.

### Registering with a factory

A factory registration is cached like any other: register it before `AddMethodCache()`, and the decorator wraps
what your factory returns, with the lifetime you chose.

```cs
builder.Services.AddScoped<IProductService>(
    sp => new ProductService(sp.GetRequiredService<Database>()));
builder.Services.AddMethodCache();
```

## What can be cached

```cs
[Cache] Product Get(int id);                          // synchronous
[Cache] Task<Product> GetAsync(int id);               // Task<T>
[Cache] ValueTask<Product> GetFastAsync(int id);      // ValueTask<T>
[Cache] Task<Product?> FindAsync(string name);        // null results are cached too
```

- Synchronous methods, `Task<T>` and `ValueTask<T>` can be cached. A method that returns nothing has nothing to
  cache, so `[Cache]` on it is a build error ([MC0003](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/user-guide/DIAGNOSTICS.md#mc0003),
  [MC0004](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/user-guide/DIAGNOSTICS.md#mc0004)). So is a lazy `IEnumerable<T>` or `IQueryable<T>`
  ([MC0015](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/user-guide/DIAGNOSTICS.md#mc0015)): return a list.
  Synchronous methods use L1/origin when the distributed adapter has no bounded native synchronous capability.
  Custom async-only managers bypass their synchronous caching path; see [Generated decorators](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/source-generator.md).
- Exceptions are never cached: the next call runs the method again.
- Concurrent calls with the same arguments share one call to your method (stampede protection). A caller that cancels
  only stops its own wait.
- Without a `Duration`, entries live five minutes (the built-in default) unless you set a
  default ([Expiration](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/expiration.md#duration)).
- `null` results are cached. Turn that off with `CacheNullValues` on the [memory cache](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/memory-cache.md), or
  per method with [conditional caching](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/conditional-caching.md).
- The cached object is returned as is, not copied. Treat cached results as read-only.

## Next steps

- Choose how long entries live: [Expiration](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/expiration.md).
- Remove entries when data changes: [Invalidation](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/invalidation.md).
- Change durations without a redeploy: [Configuration](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/configuration.md).
- Share the cache between instances: [Distributed cache](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/distributed-cache.md).

<!-- source: docs/features/source-generator.md -->

# Generated decorators

Put cache attributes on interface methods. The generator builds a decorator around the registered implementation
and routes cached calls through MethodCache. Your implementation stays ordinary application code.

The generator supports synchronous result methods, `Task<T>` and `ValueTask<T>`, overloaded methods, generic
interfaces and generic methods, including interfaces nested in generic containing types. Constraints on both
the containing type and the interface, including `unmanaged` and base class constraints, are preserved, and so are
`scoped` parameters on forwarded members. Each overload has its own
[method id](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/configuration.md#appsettingsjson) and its own cache entries.

Memory-only `Task<T>` and `ValueTask<T>` misses avoid allocating closures for inactive fail-safe and
distributed-write branches. Enabling those features retains their origin and invalidation behavior.

Public interface members are forwarded to the implementation: uncached methods, properties, indexers and events.
Non-public and sealed default interface methods stay on the interface with their own bodies; the decorator doesn't
implement them, so `[Cache]` or `[CacheInvalidate]` on one (or on a `static` member) is warning
[MC0018](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/user-guide/DIAGNOSTICS.md#mc0018). An interface with non-public abstract members is rejected with
[MC0014](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/user-guide/DIAGNOSTICS.md#mc0014), because the decorator can't call those members on the implementation.

Keywords and unusual names are escaped, and your own types named like framework types (such as `Task` or `List`)
don't clash with the generated code. You don't need to rename anything.
Long namespace and type names also work with `EmitCompilerGeneratedFiles`: the generator gives those files
short, stable names while preserving the declared types and cache identities.

Unsupported cached method shapes receive a [generator diagnostic](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/user-guide/DIAGNOSTICS.md), with a code fix
to remove the cache attribute where available. Reference returns, ref struct results and pointer/function pointer
results are rejected before cached code is emitted. Those methods are forwarded when another method on the
interface is cacheable. See [keys](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/keys.md) for argument identity and
[configuration](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/configuration.md) for generated policy identifiers.

## Registration

Generated runtime calls use the versioned `MethodCache.Generated` facade. Module initializers record descriptors
only; `AddMethodCache` validates contract versions before executing descriptors or factories. Each invocation
captures one immutable policy/prefix/publication generation, including keyed registration and background-scope
binding. A retired invocation may finish its origin call but cannot publish into the current generation.

The reviewed contract-1 surface is frozen before the first release. Generated inline keys use the bound
`KeyBuilder` constructor and `AppendPart` with ref lookups, including records, collections and key providers.
`StartKey`, `BindKey`, `KeyPrefix` and `TextKey` are internal. Compatibility checks execute the explicit
.NET 10 `Contract1Final` vendor images; earlier unpublished development checkpoints remain historical.
After release, precompiled contract-1 decorators must run on newer 1.x Core versions without regeneration.

`AddMethodCache()` wraps every registration of a cached interface in its decorator, and keeps the container's
ownership as it is: the container disposes the implementations it creates, and leaves instances you registered
yourself open. Factory registrations are wrapped the same way ([Getting started](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/getting-started.md#registering-with-a-factory)).

A factory registration for the README's `IUserService`, once `IUserDatabase` is registered:

```cs
builder.Services.AddScoped<IUserService>(sp =>
    new UserService(sp.GetRequiredService<IUserDatabase>()));
builder.Services.AddMethodCache();
```

The end-to-end signature corpus under `tests/MethodCache.SourceGenerator.IntegrationTests` checks supported shapes
with C# 12 and the latest compiler: each generated decorator compiles and runs through the actual DI registration.
It checks semantic runtime references as well. Frozen vendor binaries exercise contract compatibility without
regenerating source during ordinary tests, including under Native AOT.

`AddMethodCache` decorates explicit registrations. Missing services require explicit `AutoRegister(lifetime)`
with exactly one accessible implementation in the selected module. Use `FromAssemblyOf<T>()` when multiple
modules offer the same interface. Cacheable late, open generic, AnyKey and unsupported closed bindings fail explicitly.

Built-in synchronous methods run a synchronous factory with synchronous single-flight. They never wait on an
async loader or async refresh. Async callers can join a synchronous load. A custom async-only manager bypasses
synchronous caching and emits a diagnostic once per method/container. Current distributed adapters do not expose
bounded native synchronous operations through this path, so these calls use L1/origin and report unavailable L2;
use async methods to share results through L2. Synchronous distributed tag mutations report unsupported invalidation
after the origin/local mutation; use async mutation methods for distributed invalidation.

The attribute-move code fix preserves semantic binding across scopes and files: attribute/type aliases are qualified as needed, and constant arguments are materialized before they leave an implementation class.

With C# 13 or newer, generated decorators preserve `allows ref struct` constraints when the cached values and arguments themselves are ordinary cacheable types. Potentially ref-like type parameters used as cache arguments or results receive MC0009 instead of broken generated code. The packages require .NET 10 and the .NET 10 SDK. C# 12 source remains supported when explicitly selected in that SDK.

<!-- source: docs/features/keys.md -->

# Cache keys

You never write keys for `[Cache]` methods. The generated decorator builds each key from the interface, the method
and the arguments, so two calls share an entry exactly when they call the same method with equal arguments.

Chapter 10 of the [console demo](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/samples/MethodCache.Demo) includes the tenant ID in both the key
and the invalidation tag, keeping the same product ID separate for two tenants. Derive that tenant from an
authorized identity in an application; cache-key separation does not authorize access.

```cs
public sealed record UserQuery(string Name, int Page);

public interface IUserService
{
    [Cache] Task<User> GetAsync(int id);                     // [MyApp]MyApp.IUserService.GetAsync:42
    [Cache] Task<List<User>> SearchAsync(UserQuery query);   // [MyApp]MyApp.IUserService.SearchAsync:(alice:2)
    [Cache] Task<List<User>> ByIdsAsync(int[] ids);          // [MyApp]MyApp.IUserService.ByIdsAsync:[3:1:2:3]
    [Cache] Task<int> CountAsync(Dictionary<string, int[]> filters); // [MyApp]MyApp.IUserService.CountAsync:{hash} (hashed)
}
```

Examples below assume the service assembly is named `MyApp`. Its simple name prefixes every key as `[MyApp]`;
assembly versions are excluded, so redeploying a new version preserves key identity. Closed generic argument types
also include their assembly identity. Assemblies with the same namespace/type names therefore keep separate entries.
Assembly-name characters outside letters, digits, `.`, `_` and `-` are escaped as `%XXXX` UTF-16 code units.
Use `IMethodCacheKeys` to get the exact key of a call ([Building a key yourself](#building-a-key-yourself)); the admin method list shows the method ids configuration uses.

## How arguments become keys

- **Simple values** (strings, numbers, `bool`, `Guid`, dates, enums) are written as they are: `GetAsync:42`.
- **Records, classes and structs** whose public properties and fields are simple values are written field by field:
  `SearchAsync:(alice:2)`. Two records with equal values give the same key.
- **Types that implement `ICacheKeyProvider`** contribute their `CacheKeyPart`.
- **Arrays and collections** of those values are written with their count and then each element in order:
  `ByIdsAsync:[3:1:2:3]`. Records and classes inside a collection must be sealed, since an unsealed element type
  could hold a subclass with more members. A dictionary counts when its keys and values are simple values. When a
  collection's runtime type differs from its declared type (an array or a list passed as `IEnumerable<int>`), the key
  includes that type, so an array and a list with the same elements stay two entries. Unknown collection subclasses passed through a base class or interface use the key generator so their own runtime state is preserved.
- **Collection subclasses with public state**, such as a list with a tenant or scope property, use the key generator. Their keys include both that public state and the elements, including when the collection is behind a base-class property. This applies to the internal fallback generator.
- **Everything else**, such as an interface or `object` argument or a collection of collections, goes through the key
  generator. The internal default generator hashes the arguments into a key such as `CountAsync:fc08ab0d…`.
- **Framework types** are written by their value wherever they appear, not by their public properties; see
  [Framework types](#framework-types). Other framework types are a build error.
- **`nint` and `nuint`** also go through the key generator, as the 64-bit number they hold, so a value gets the same
  key in 32-bit and 64-bit processes. Their type is kept: `(nint)1`, `1` and `1L` are three keys, also inside an
  `object[]` or an `object` property.
- **Values inside hashed arguments keep their runtime type.** Where a value's type differs from the type it is declared
  as (an element of `object[]` or `List<object>`, an `object` property, a property typed as a base class or interface),
  the key records the value's version-independent assembly/type identity and all of its members: `new object[] { 1 }` and `new object[] { 1L }` get
  different keys, and so do two `Circle`s behind a `Shape` property that differ only in `Radius`.
- A `CancellationToken` parameter is never part of the key.
- Keys don't depend on the current culture: `-1`, `1.5` and dates are written the same under every culture.
- `0.0` and `-0.0` are two keys in every key form (`1 / x` tells them apart). `NaN` and the infinities work anywhere,
  also inside a hashed argument, such as `double.PositiveInfinity` as a "no limit" value in a filter record.

On .NET 10 the decorator writes simple keys into a stack buffer and looks them up without allocating.

## Types whose state is private

A type with only private state, including private fields inherited from a base class, would give every value the
same key, so the key generators refuse it with an
`InvalidOperationException` instead of returning wrong results. This holds wherever the type appears in an argument:
as the argument itself, as a property of a record, or as an element of an array, list or dictionary. Implement
`ICacheKeyProvider` on it, or give it public properties:

```cs
public sealed class TenantId(Guid value) : ICacheKeyProvider
{
    private readonly Guid _value = value;   // private state: MethodCache can't see it

    public string CacheKeyPart => _value.ToString("N");
}
```

## Framework types

Types from .NET itself often keep their value out of their public properties (`BigInteger` has `IsZero` and
`Sign`, `IPAddress.ScopeId` throws for IPv4), so writing those would give different values one key. These go through
the key generator, which writes their value, in an argument of their own or inside a record, collection or tuple:

- `Guid`, `DateTime`, `DateTimeOffset`, `TimeSpan`, `DateOnly`, `TimeOnly`
- `Half`, `Int128`, `UInt128`, `BigInteger`, `Complex`
- `Uri`, `Version`, `IPAddress` (`IPAddress.Loopback` and `IPAddress.Parse("127.0.0.1")` share a key)
- `JsonElement`, as its JSON, so `{"a":1}` and `{ "a": 1 }` share a key
- `Index`, `Range`, `Vector2`, `Vector3`, `Vector4`, `Quaternion`, `Plane`, `Matrix3x2`, `Matrix4x4`
- ASP.NET Core's `PathString`, `QueryString` and `HostString`
- arrays, collections, `Memory<T>`, `Tuple`, `ValueTuple` and `KeyValuePair` of these

Any other type from .NET itself, ASP.NET Core or Microsoft.Extensions in a key (one from an assembly named
`System.*`, `Microsoft.AspNetCore.*` or `Microsoft.Extensions.*`), such as `StringBuilder` (which can change after
the call), `CultureInfo`, `Stream`, `Type` or a delegate, is build error
[MC0019](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/user-guide/DIAGNOSTICS.md#mc0019), also as a property of your own record. Pass a value that identifies
it, such as `culture.Name`, or wrap it in a type that implements `ICacheKeyProvider`. Other libraries' models, such
as an SDK's classes in a `Microsoft.*` namespace, are written by their public properties like your own types.

## Key construction and value serialization

Key construction belongs to the runtime. Complex arguments use the internal canonical encoder; custom key parts use
`ICacheKeyProvider`. JSON and MessagePack settings select distributed **value** serialization and do not replace the
key generator.

```cs
builder.Services.AddMethodCache(cache => cache.UseJson());
```

## Method scope

Generated keys always include the assembly simple name, interface, method, version, closed generic types, the implementation type when an interface has several registrations, and the service key of a keyed registration. An argument cannot replace that scope: `CacheKeyAttribute` and its `UseAsRawKey` flag have been removed. Use `ICacheKeyProvider` to customize one argument's part, or the manual `ICacheManager` API when supplying a complete key.

```cs
public interface IDocumentStore
{
    // The document path is an argument; the interface and method remain part of the key.
    [Cache] Task<byte[]> GetAsync(string key);
}
```

## Building a key yourself

To invalidate or inspect one entry, ask `IMethodCacheKeys` for the key of the call. Resolve it from dependency
injection; the compiler checks the call, so overloads, versions, generic methods and argument formatting can't be
gotten wrong:

```cs
var key = keys.For<IOrderService>(orders => orders.GetAsync(42));
await cache.InvalidateKeyAsync(key);   // "[MyApp]Docs.Invalidation.IOrderService.GetAsync:42"
```

```cs
// A method with a Version: "[MyApp]MyApp.IInvoiceService.GetAsync:v2:42"
var versioned = keys.For<IInvoiceService>(invoices => invoices.GetAsync(42));

// An overloaded method: "[MyApp]MyApp.IInvoiceService.FindAsync(string):INV-7"
var overload = keys.For<IInvoiceService>(invoices => invoices.FindAsync("INV-7"));
```

`For` runs the call on a stand-in that records the key the decorator would use, under the method's current policy, so
it also follows a runtime version change. The method itself never runs. The call must reach exactly one cached method;
anything else, such as a method without `[Cache]`, throws an `InvalidOperationException`. For a keyed registration,
pass its service key: `keys.For<IRates>(rates => rates.Get("EUR"), serviceKey: "ecb")`.

To work with every entry of one method, ask for its method id instead. It is the id the admin method list shows and
appsettings uses, and it covers all arguments, versions, generic arguments and keyed registrations of the method:

```cs
// "[MyApp]MyApp.IInvoiceService.FindAsync(string)": the arguments don't matter
var methodId = keys.MethodId<IInvoiceService>(invoices => invoices.FindAsync(""));
var entries = admin.ListEntries(methodId: methodId);
```

```cs
var methodId = keys.MethodId<IInvoiceService>(invoices => invoices.FindAsync(""));
var result = await admin.InvalidateMethodAsync(methodId);   // every result of the method, on every instance
```

`CacheEntryInfo.MethodId` tells which method an entry belongs to; it is `null` for entries stored through
`ICacheManager` directly. An application `ICacheManager` stores entries under `MethodCacheKeys.StoredKey(key, version)`;
see [Manual caching](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/manual-caching.md).

## Things to know

- **Keys contain the arguments.** Don't cache methods that take secrets such as passwords or tokens as arguments; pass
  an identifier instead. Hashed keys are not encryption. No argument, whatever characters it contains, can produce
  another call's key; see [Security](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/security.md).
- **`Version` changes every key** of a method, so values cached by an earlier version are ignored. See
  [Expiration](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/expiration.md#versions).
- **Overloaded methods** have their parameter types in their keys, so overloads never share entries. See
  [method ids](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/configuration.md#appsettingsjson).
- **A method name that another interface in the hierarchy also declares** gets the same treatment. Keys start with
  the decorated interface, so for `ICatalog : ILookup` with `ILookup.Find(int)` and `ICatalog.Find(string)` the keys
  are `[MyApp]MyApp.ICatalog.Find(int):7` and `[MyApp]MyApp.ICatalog.Find(string):7`. When two base interfaces declare the same
  signature, the declaring interface is added too: for `IC : IA, IB` that both declare `Get(int)`, the keys are
  `[MyApp]MyApp.IC.[MyApp]MyApp.IA.Get(int):1` and `[MyApp]MyApp.IC.[MyApp]MyApp.IB.Get(int):1`. Policy ids don't change; each
  method keeps the id of the interface that declares it.
- **Keyed registrations** have their service key after the method name, so `AddKeyedScoped<IRates, EcbRates>("ecb")`
  and `AddKeyedScoped<IRates, FedRates>("fed")` each cache their own results: `[MyApp]MyApp.IRates.Get@ecb:1` and
  `[MyApp]MyApp.IRates.Get@fed:1`. Other keys carry their type (`Get@[MyApp]MyApp.Region.Eu`, `Get@Int32(7)`), and a
  string with a `.`, `(` or `"` in it is written in quotes, so keys of different types never share entries. The service
  key must be a string, enum, bool, char, integer or `Guid`; `AddMethodCache()` throws for a keyed registration of a
  cached interface with any other key, and for a `KeyedService.AnyKey` registration. A constructor parameter marked
  `[ServiceKey]` receives your key, as it does without MethodCache.
- **Several registrations of one interface** under the same service key (or under none) with different
  implementation types each cache their own results. Their keys carry the implementation type before any service key:
  with `AddSingleton<IRates, EcbRates>()` and `AddSingleton<IRates, FedRates>()` the keys are
  `[MyApp]MyApp.IRates.Get#[MyApp]MyApp.EcbRates:1` and `[MyApp]MyApp.IRates.Get#[MyApp]MyApp.FedRates:1`. A single
  registration keeps the plain key. Two registrations the container builds from the same implementation type, such as
  a library and the application both calling `AddSingleton<IRates, EcbRates>()`, are interchangeable and share their
  results. An instance registration can be configured differently, so `AddMethodCache()` fails when one has the same
  type as another registration under that key; a factory that creates the same type as another registration fails
  when both have been created. Give each its own service key instead. `keys.For<IRates>(...)` returns the key of the
  last registration, the one `GetService<IRates>()` returns.
- **All registrations of a method share its method id and its tags.** A `[CacheInvalidate]` tag, on any registration,
  and `InvalidateMethodAsync` remove the matching entries of all of them.
- **Generic methods** carry their closed type arguments after the method name, before any implementation type or
  service key: `Get<[System.Private.CoreLib]System.Int32>:1`. Overloads that differ only in generic arity stay apart in
  ids and keys: `Get(int)`, ``Get`1(int)`` and ``Get`2(int)``. `keys.For` writes the type arguments for you, and the
  method id covers every closed type.
- To see the keys your application produces, list them with `ICacheAdministrator.ListEntries()` or the admin
  endpoints ([Monitoring](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/monitoring.md)).


---

<!-- source: docs/features/expiration.md -->

# Expiration

Each cached method decides how long its entries live. The settings below can be set on `[Cache]`, in startup code, in
`appsettings.json` or at runtime ([Configuration](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/configuration.md)).

Chapter 7 of the [console demo](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/samples/MethodCache.Demo) runs absolute expiry, sliding windows and
refresh-ahead with an explicitly advanced clock and checked source-call counts.

```cs
public interface IReportService
{
    // Gone ten minutes after it was stored
    [Cache(Duration = "00:10:00")]
    Task<Report> GetAsync(int year);

    // Kept while it is read at least every five minutes, but never longer than an hour
    [Cache(Duration = "01:00:00", SlidingExpiration = "00:05:00")]
    Task<Session> GetSessionAsync(string id);

    // Reloaded in the background when it is read in its last minute, so callers never wait
    [Cache(Duration = "00:10:00", RefreshAhead = "00:01:00")]
    Task<PriceList> GetPricesAsync(string region);

    // Changing the version changes every key, so values cached by the previous version are ignored
    [Cache(Duration = "1.00:00:00", Version = 2)]
    Task<Report> GetYearlyAsync(int year);
}
```

Durations accept an invariant positive decimal followed by `s`, `m`, `h` or `d` (case-insensitive), or `[d.]hh:mm:ss` with up to seven fractional second digits. Examples: `"30s"`, `"1.5h"`, `"1.00:00:00"`. Outer whitespace is ignored. The result must be an exact positive whole number of ticks; fractional ticks are rejected. Bare integers, zero, negatives, exponents, decimal commas, combined units and overflow are errors. The same parser is used for attributes and configuration; invalid explicit attributes produce [MC0004](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/user-guide/DIAGNOSTICS.md#mc0004) even without analyzers. `SlidingExpiration`, `RefreshAhead` and `FailSafe` also accept `"off"`, and `TimeSpan.Zero` in the builder (`WithSlidingExpiration`, `WithRefreshAhead`, `WithFailSafe`) does the same. Timeout and retry windows must stay positive.

## Duration

`Duration` is how long an entry lives after it was stored. A method without one uses the global default:

```cs
builder.Services.AddMethodCache(config =>
    config.Defaults(o => o.WithDuration(TimeSpan.FromMinutes(15))));
```

Without any default, entries live for five minutes. No entry lives
longer than `MethodCacheMemoryOptions.MaxExpiration` (seven days). See [Memory cache](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/memory-cache.md).

## Sliding expiration

`SlidingExpiration` keeps an entry while it is read: each read extends its life by the sliding window. It never lives
past its `Duration`; without a `Duration`, only `MaxExpiration` limits it.

A method that inherits a sliding window from the defaults, a group or configuration turns it off with
`SlidingExpiration = "off"` (`TimeSpan.Zero` in code). Leaving the setting out inherits it. `RefreshAhead` works the
same way.

## Refresh-ahead

`RefreshAhead` reloads an entry in the background when it is read within that window before it expires. The caller
gets the cached value at once, and the reload replaces it, so a popular entry never makes anyone wait. An entry that
isn't read in the window simply expires.

The window must be shorter than `Duration` and `SlidingExpiration`, or every read would reload the entry: on `[Cache]`
(build error [MC0023](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/user-guide/DIAGNOSTICS.md#mc0023)), in code (`Build()` throws an `InvalidOperationException`)
and in `appsettings.json` (startup fails) a longer one is rejected.
When settings from different places combine into such a window, for example an attribute's `RefreshAhead` with a
shorter `Duration` from configuration, the reload starts halfway through the entry's life instead.

The reload outlives the request that triggered it. For a service registered as scoped or transient (a repository
with a scoped `DbContext`, say), it runs on a new instance from a new DI scope, which is disposed when the reload ends,
never on the request's instance, whose scope may already be gone. That instance has none of the request's state: no
`HttpContext`, and no values the request set on the instance or in `AsyncLocal`. Each scoped or transient cached
service the reload calls gets an instance this way, also from a manual `GetOrCreateAsync` factory, and every scope is
disposed when the reload ends; a call the factory leaves running after it returned keeps the instance it was given.
Singletons reload on their one instance. A `CancellationToken` parameter of the method still cancels the reload.

## Versions

`Version` is part of every key the method produces. Raise it when the shape of the cached result changes, for example
after adding a property, so values cached by the previous deployment are never returned. The old entries expire on
their own.

## Spreading out expiry

Entries created at the same moment, for example right after a deploy, also expire together.
`MethodCacheMemoryOptions.JitterMaxDuration` adds a random extra lifetime to each entry to spread them out
([Memory cache](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/memory-cache.md)).

## Removing entries early

> [!TIP]
> Expiration is for data that may be a little old. When you know data changed, remove it right away with
> [invalidation](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/invalidation.md).


---

<!-- source: docs/features/invalidation.md -->

# Invalidation

Expiration removes entries eventually; invalidation removes them the moment you know the data changed.

## Tags

Give cached methods tags, and list the same tags on the methods that change the data:

```cs
public interface IOrderService
{
    [Cache(Duration = "00:10:00", Tags = ["orders", "order:{orderId}"])]
    Task<Order> GetAsync(int orderId);

    [Cache(Duration = "00:05:00", Tags = ["orders", "customer:{customerId}:orders", "customer:{customerId}"])]
    Task<List<Order>> ListForCustomerAsync(int customerId);

    // Removes this order and the customer's list, nothing else
    [CacheInvalidate(Tags = ["order:{orderId}", "customer:{customerId}:orders", "customer:{customerId}"])]
    Task CancelAsync(int orderId, int customerId);

    // Removes every cached order
    [CacheInvalidate(Tags = ["orders"])]
    Task ImportAsync(Stream file);
}
```

- `[CacheInvalidate]` removes every entry with any of its tags once the method has completed successfully. If it
  throws, nothing is removed.
- A tag can be shared by many methods, so one write clears every cached view of the same data.
- `[CacheInvalidate]` without tags removes nothing and is reported as [MC0007](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/user-guide/DIAGNOSTICS.md#mc0007).

## Tag templates

`"order:{orderId}"` is filled in from the method's arguments: `GetAsync(42)` is tagged `order:42`, and
`CancelAsync(42, 7)` removes `order:42`. The name in braces must be a parameter of the method it is on. The exact
spelling is used first; otherwise a single case-insensitive match is used. A name that matches several parameters
only by case, such as `{NAME}` for `name` and `Name`, stays literal text and is reported as
[MC0017](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/user-guide/DIAGNOSTICS.md#mc0017). An unknown name is reported as
[MC0010](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/user-guide/DIAGNOSTICS.md#mc0010), with a code fix that offers the closest parameter. Arguments use canonical key-part formatting: strings escape backslashes and colons, GUIDs use the 32-digit `N`
format, and null uses `\0`. Braces in an argument remain literal: an id of `"{org}"` gives
the tag `order:{org}` on both the cached call and the invalidation.

A template takes a parameter name only. `"{order.Id}"` is not a template and stays literal text, so every call would
share one tag; it is reported as [MC0016](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/user-guide/DIAGNOSTICS.md#mc0016). Add the id as a parameter, as `UpdateAsync(int id, Product product)` does in
[Getting started](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/getting-started.md).

Static tags never format method arguments. A template formats only the parameters it references, in the invariant culture; an unrelated argument's `ToString()` is not invoked.

Tags set in startup code, `appsettings.json` or runtime overrides can use templates too, with any parameter of the
method. They are added to the `[Cache]` attribute's tags, so the attribute's `[CacheInvalidate]` tags keep working;
only an explicit `ClearTags()` (or `"ClearTags": true` in `appsettings.json`) replaces them
([Configuration](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/configuration.md)). An override with `o => o.AddTags("incident")` on `GetAsync` above gives its
entries the tags `orders`, `order:{orderId}` and `incident`.

`[CacheInvalidate]` also works on methods with `ref` or `ref readonly` returns, and on `Task` and `ValueTask` methods
with `ref`, `out` or `in` parameters. The tags are filled in after the call returns, and the entries are removed only
once the task has completed successfully.

## From code

`ICacheManager` invalidates by tag or by key:

```cs
await cache.InvalidateTagsAsync(["order:42", "customer:7:orders"]);
```

```cs
var key = keys.For<IOrderService>(orders => orders.GetAsync(42));
await cache.InvalidateKeyAsync(key);   // "[MyApp]Docs.Invalidation.IOrderService.GetAsync:42"
```

```cs
await cache.InvalidateTagAsync("customer:7");   // add this tag to every customer entry
```

- `IMethodCacheKeys.For` returns the key the generated decorator uses for that call, including overloads, versions,
  generic methods and keyed registrations; resolve `IMethodCacheKeys` from dependency injection. See
  [Building a key yourself](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/keys.md#building-a-key-yourself).
- Invalidation matches exact tags and keys; there are no wildcard patterns. Attach a common tag to all entries in a
  group instead.
- To remove every entry of one method, pass its id to `ICacheAdministrator.InvalidateMethodAsync`; get the id from
  `IMethodCacheKeys.MethodId` ([Cache keys](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/keys.md#building-a-key-yourself)).
- The admin endpoints and `ICacheAdministrator` also invalidate by tag and by method ([Monitoring](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/monitoring.md)).

## With several instances

With [Redis or SQL Server](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/distributed-cache.md), invalidating a tag or key removes it from the distributed cache and
tells every instance to drop its in-memory copy. You don't need to do anything else.


---

<!-- source: docs/features/fail-safe.md -->

# Fail-safe

Fail-safe keeps an expired value for a while and returns it when calling the method again fails, so a database or API
outage shows slightly old data instead of errors. It is off by default.

Chapter 8 of the [console demo](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/samples/MethodCache.Demo) shows a failing API, retry suppression,
recovery and a slow response that finishes after the caller receives its fallback. A fake clock controls the
expiry, retry and timeout windows; the same scenario runs in the docs tests.

## Turning it on

For every cached method at once:

```cs
builder.Services.AddMethodCache(config => config.Defaults(o => o
    .WithFailSafe(TimeSpan.FromHours(1))                    // how long an expired value is kept as a fallback
    .WithFailSafeTimeout(TimeSpan.FromMilliseconds(200))    // optional: don't wait longer than this when a fallback exists
    .WithFailSafeRetryAfter(TimeSpan.FromSeconds(30))));    // optional: reuse the fallback this long before trying again
```

or in `appsettings.json`:

```json
{
  "MethodCache": {
    "FailSafe": { "Duration": "01:00:00", "Timeout": "00:00:00.200", "RetryAfter": "00:00:30" }
  }
}
```

## What happens

- **When the method throws**, the caller gets the expired value if it is younger than the fail-safe duration. That
  value is then reused for the retry delay (`RetryAfter`, default 30 seconds) before the method is called again, so a
  failing dependency isn't hammered; no [refresh-ahead](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/expiration.md#refresh-ahead) reload starts during that time
  either.
- **When the method is slow** and a `Timeout` is set, the caller gets the expired value after it and the call
  finishes in the background; its result replaces the old value. Without an expired value the caller waits as usual.
  Because the call may outlive the request, a scoped or transient service makes it on a new instance from a new DI
  scope, disposed when the call ends, whenever a fallback exists and a `Timeout` is set (the instance has none of the
  request's own state, such as values set on the instance). The caller's `HttpContext` and `AsyncLocal` values still
  flow to it, as it starts on the caller's call. Singletons use their one instance.
- A caller's own cancellation is never treated as a failure, so it doesn't trigger fail-safe.
- A value that was invalidated (its key, a tag or a clear) or replaced is never a fallback, also when that happened
  while the reload ran: callers then wait for the reload, or get its exception.
- Without an expired value, the exception reaches the caller as usual.
- `GetOrCreateManyAsync` works the same way for each key: when the batch factory throws, each key gets its own
  fallback, and the exception is thrown only when a key has none.

## Per method

A method or group can change any of it, and its own setting wins over the central one. `[Cache]` takes the same three
settings as `FailSafe`, `FailSafeTimeout` and `FailSafeRetryAfter`:

```cs
public interface IAccountService
{
    [Cache(Duration = "00:05:00", FailSafe = "01:00:00", FailSafeTimeout = "00:00:00.200")]
    Task<Rates> GetRatesAsync();

    [Cache(FailSafe = "off")]   // a balance must never be old, so an error is better
    Task<decimal> GetBalanceAsync(int accountId);
}
```

In code, use the builder methods with the same names: `WithFailSafe`, `WithFailSafeTimeout` and
`WithFailSafeRetryAfter`, for example `Configure(o => o.WithFailSafeTimeout(TimeSpan.FromMilliseconds(100)))` to
change only the timeout. `o.WithFailSafe(TimeSpan.Zero)` turns fail-safe off. In `appsettings.json`, a method takes
`FailSafe` (a time span or `"off"`), `FailSafeTimeout` and `FailSafeRetryAfter`.

## Limits

> [!NOTE]
> The fallback lives in each instance's memory, so right after a restart there is none until the method has succeeded
> once.

Caller cancellation stops the wait during an L2 read or a slow factory, including bulk reads and fail-safe waits. L2 reads pass cancellation to the backend; shared factory work may finish for other callers. Caller cancellation is not reported as a dependency failure.


---

<!-- source: docs/features/conditional-caching.md -->

# Conditional caching

Sometimes a result should be returned but not remembered: an empty search, a product that doesn't exist yet, a
response that says "try again later".

Chapter 9 of the [console demo](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/samples/MethodCache.Demo) skips missing products and proves that a
newly created product is visible on the next lookup, while existing products are cached.

## CacheWhen

`CacheWhen` stores a result only when the predicate returns true:

```cs
builder.Services.AddMethodCache(config =>
{
    // Don't remember empty search results: the next search asks the database again
    config.Method((IProductService s) => s.SearchAsync(Any<string>.Value))
          .CacheWhen(results => results.Count > 0);

    // A product that doesn't exist yet may be created any moment
    config.Method((IProductService s) => s.FindAsync(Any<int>.Value))
          .CacheWhen(product => product is not null);
});
```

- A rejected result is still returned to the caller, and the next call runs the method again.
- The entry it would have replaced, including a fail-safe value, stays.
- The predicate runs once per load, and on each value read from the distributed cache: a value it rejects there is
  skipped and the method runs. It never runs on a hit in memory. If it throws, the result is returned and not stored.
- `config.Method(...).CacheWhen` gets the method's result type. A `CacheWhen<T>` set elsewhere for a type the method
  can't return, such as `CacheWhen<string>` on a method that returns `int`, makes the call throw an
  `InvalidOperationException` instead of silently caching nothing.
- It is set for one method in code only, so it can't come from `appsettings.json`. In `Defaults` or a group it fails
  at startup. `.CacheWhen(...)` and `.Configure(o => o.CacheWhen<T>(...))` set the same thing: the last call wins.
  `Any<T>.Value` stands for any argument.

> [!TIP]
> To stop caching `null` everywhere, set `CacheNullValues = false` on the [memory cache](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/memory-cache.md) instead.

## Skipping the cache for one call

With [manual caching](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/manual-caching.md), `WithEnabled` decides per call whether to use the cache at all:

```cs
var results = await cache.GetOrCreateAsync(
    $"search:{text}",
    async ct => await search(),
    o => o.WithDuration(TimeSpan.FromMinutes(10))
          .WithEnabled(!preview));   // preview requests skip the cache entirely
```

With `WithEnabled(false)`, the factory runs and its result is neither read from nor written to the cache.
To decide from the result instead, use `CacheWhen` ([Validation](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/configuration.md#validation)).


---

<!-- source: docs/features/configuration.md -->

# Configuration

A cached method's policy (duration, sliding expiration, refresh-ahead, fail-safe, tags, group, version) can come from
four layers. Change it in `appsettings.json` or at runtime, and the next call uses it, without a redeploy.

| Layer | How you set it | Priority | Changes while running |
|-------|----------------|----------|-----------------------|
| Attributes | `[Cache(...)]` on the interface method | 10 (lowest) | No |
| Startup code | `AddMethodCache(config => ...)` | 40 | No |
| Configuration | `AddMethodCache(b => b.FromConfiguration(configuration))` | 50 | Yes, when the configuration reloads |
| Runtime overrides | `IRuntimeCacheConfigurator` | 100 (highest) | Yes |

When several layers configure the same method, they are merged setting by setting, and the highest layer that sets a
setting wins. A runtime override of `Duration` leaves the attribute's `Tags` in place.

Tags are the exception: they are combined, not replaced. Tags from startup code, `appsettings.json`, runtime overrides
and the defaults are added to the `[Cache]` attribute's tags (without duplicates), so a `[CacheInvalidate]` that
lists an attribute tag always reaches the entry. To replace the tags instead, call `ClearTags()` before `AddTags`
(`o => o.ClearTags().AddTags("orders")`), or set `"ClearTags": true` next to `Tags` for a method in
`appsettings.json`. The tags of the lower layers and of the defaults are then dropped, and an entry without them is
no longer removed by a `[CacheInvalidate]` that lists them.

## Defaults and groups

Within the layers, each setting comes from the most specific place that sets it: the method itself, then its group,
then the defaults.

```cs
builder.Services.AddMethodCache(config =>
{
    // Every cached method: fills in what the method leaves unset
    config.Defaults(o => o.WithDuration(TimeSpan.FromMinutes(15)));

    // Methods in the "user-data" group: [Cache(Group = "user-data")] or WithGroup("user-data")
    config.Group("user-data", o => o.WithSlidingExpiration(TimeSpan.FromMinutes(10)));

    // One method
    config.Method((IUserService s) => s.GetProfileAsync(Any<int>.Value))
          .Configure(o => o.WithDuration(TimeSpan.FromHours(2)).WithRefreshAhead(TimeSpan.FromMinutes(5)));
});
```

- `Defaults` applies to every cached method, also ones that only have `[Cache]`. `[Cache(Duration = "00:10:00")]`
  keeps its ten minutes while the defaults fill in what it leaves out.
- A method joins a group with `[Cache(Group = "name")]`, `WithGroup("name")` in code, or `Group` in `appsettings.json`.
  Group names are case-sensitive. A group's defaults come from `config.Group(...)` and from `"Groups"` in
  `appsettings.json`, which wins where both set a value; a method's own settings win over both.
- `CacheWhen` is set for one method only. In `Defaults` or a group it fails at startup
  ([Conditional caching](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/conditional-caching.md)).
- `Any<T>.Value` stands for any argument when you point at a method.

Startup uses `MethodCacheBuilder`: `Defaults`, `Group`, typed `Method` expressions, `Memory`, `Distributed`,
`Telemetry`, `FromConfiguration`, `FromAssemblyOf` and explicit `AutoRegister(lifetime)`. Redis, SQL Server and
MessagePack packages add `UseRedis`, `UseSqlServer` and `UseMessagePack`; Core provides `UseJson`. Use one
distributed cache: `UseRedis` and `UseSqlServer` together throw. `Distributed(...)`, `UseMessagePack` or `UseJson`
without a distributed cache logs a warning, since they have nothing to apply to. `builder.Services` is the service
collection, for a package that adds its own `UseXxx` method.
`Method` on a method without `[Cache]` fails at startup, and on a method that returns nothing (`void`, `Task`,
`ValueTask`) throws an `ArgumentException`.
All integration packages require the exact same Core package version; do not override this bound.
CI uses strict restore (NU1608 as an error) to reject direct-version overrides. Configure services before `AddMethodCache`.
Runtime overrides use the same immutable options builder as startup and manual cache calls.

## appsettings.json

```cs
builder.Services.AddMethodCache(methodCache => methodCache.FromConfiguration(builder.Configuration));   // the "MethodCache" section
```

```json
{
  "MethodCache": {
    "Defaults": { "Duration": "00:15:00" },
    "FailSafe": { "Duration": "01:00:00" },
    "Groups": {
      "user-data": { "SlidingExpiration": "00:10:00" }
    },
    "Methods": {
      "[MyApp]MyApp.IUserService.GetProfileAsync": {
        "Duration": "01:00:00",
        "SlidingExpiration": "00:10:00",
        "RefreshAhead": "00:05:00",
        "Tags": ["users"],
        "Version": 1,
        "Notes": "Profiles change rarely"
      },
      "[MyApp]MyApp.IAccountService.GetBalanceAsync": { "FailSafe": "off" }
    }
  }
}
```

- Each key under `Methods` is the **method id**: the escaped assembly simple name in brackets, the full interface name, a dot and the method name (for example `[MyApp]MyApp.IUserService.GetProfileAsync`). Assembly versions do not participate. A generic
  interface is written with its type parameters (`[MyApp]MyApp.IRepository<T>.GetAsync`), and an overloaded method adds its
  parameter types (`[MyApp]MyApp.IUserService.FindAsync(int)`). Parameter types other than built-in ones are qualified by
  namespace (`[MyApp]MyApp.IUsers.Find(MyApp.Request)`), so overloads taking `A.Request` and `B.Request` stay separate. Types
  are named as reflection sees them: a tuple is `System.ValueTuple<int, string>` (element names dropped), `nint` is
  `System.IntPtr` and `dynamic` is `object`. Runtime overrides by method id use the same format, and the parameter
  list is also part of the method's cache keys. The admin endpoints list every method id ([Monitoring](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/monitoring.md)),
  and `IMethodCacheKeys.MethodId<T>(s => s.FindAsync(0))` returns the id of a call ([Cache keys](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/keys.md)).
- Settings: `Duration`, `SlidingExpiration`, `RefreshAhead` and `FailSafe` (each but `Duration` a time span or `"off"`), `FailSafeTimeout`,
  `FailSafeRetryAfter`, `Tags`, `Version`, `Enabled` and `Distributed`. A group under `Groups` and a method under
  `Methods` can also set `ClearTags` (`true` or `false`): `true` makes their `Tags` replace the lower layers' instead of
  adding to them. Only a method can set `Group`, `Metadata` and `Notes`; in `Defaults` or a group they are an error.
  `Metadata` and `Notes` are recorded for diagnostics and never change caching; to put a method in a group, use
  `Group`. Names are case-insensitive; any other name is an error, so a misspelled `"Durration"` is reported
  instead of ignored. The same goes for the section itself: it holds only `Defaults`, `FailSafe`, `Groups` and
  `Methods`. A leftover `Services` section from 1.0.0-rc.1 is reported as an unknown setting.
- Tag templates such as `"order:{orderId}"` are checked against the parameters of every method they reach, as for
  `[Cache]` ([MC0010](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/user-guide/DIAGNOSTICS.md#mc0010)): a template that names a parameter a method doesn't have
  fails at startup.
- Durations use the same invariant grammar as attributes: positive unit values such as `"30s"` or `"1.5h"`,
  or `"hh:mm:ss"` (including `"d.hh:mm:ss"`). A bare number such as `"300"` is rejected rather than interpreted as days. `Tags` is a list (`["users"]`), and a method's `FailSafe` is one time span: the
  `{ "Duration", "Timeout", "RetryAfter" }` block exists only at the top of the section. Setting the same value in
  that block and in `Defaults` (for example `FailSafe.Timeout` and `Defaults.FailSafeTimeout`) is an error.
- A method can also be listed under an index with a `MethodId` property. Environment variable names can't hold `.`,
  `(` or `<`, so this is how environment variables, Kubernetes `env` or Linux App Service configure a method:

  ```bash
  MethodCache__Methods__0__MethodId="[MyApp]MyApp.IUserService.FindAsync(int)"
  MethodCache__Methods__0__Duration="00:02:00"
  ```

  A method can be listed once. Listing it both by name and under an index, for example by name in
  `appsettings.json` and under an index in an environment variable, fails at startup and names both paths. To
  override one file's settings from another source, list the method under the same index in both.
- `Defaults` applies to every cached method; the top-level `FailSafe` section is described in [Fail-safe](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/fail-safe.md).
- Pass a section name as the second argument to read another section. Environment files such as
  `appsettings.Production.json` work as usual. The section is read when the host starts, so configuration sources
  added after `FromConfiguration`, such as a later `AddJsonFile` or a `WebApplicationFactory`'s test
  settings, apply from the first call.
- Changes apply while the application runs, as soon as the configuration reloads (`appsettings.json` reloads on save
  by default).
- Only methods with `[Cache]` (or listed in `[assembly: CacheInterface]`) have a decorator, so the file can change
  their policy but can't make other methods cached. A method id that matches no cached method, such as a misspelled
  name or an id without its `[Assembly]` prefix, fails at startup and suggests the closest cached id. `*` and
  `group:<name>` are not method ids; use `Defaults` and `Groups`.
- An invalid value, such as a `Duration` that isn't a positive time span, makes the host fail to start with an
  `InvalidOperationException` naming the setting (without a generic host, the first cached call throws). If a
  reloaded file has one, the reload is logged as an error naming the setting's path, never its value, and the
  previous policies stay.

## Runtime overrides

A runtime override of a method wins over that method's other layers (its attribute, startup code and
`appsettings.json`). Use them to change a policy without a deploy, for example to shorten a duration during an
incident:

```cs
var configurator = app.Services.GetRequiredService<IRuntimeCacheConfigurator>();

// One method, strongly typed, with who and why for the audit trail
await configurator.UpsertAsync<IOrdersService>(
    s => s.GetAsync(Any<int>.Value),
    o => o.WithDuration(TimeSpan.FromMinutes(2)),
    new RuntimeOverrideMetadata { Owner = "ops", Reason = "Incident 4211", ExpiresAt = DateTimeOffset.UtcNow.AddHours(4) });

// By method id, for example from an admin form
await configurator.UpsertAsync($"[{typeof(IUserService).Assembly.GetName().Name}]Docs.Configuration.IUserService.GetProfileAsync",
    o => o.WithDuration(TimeSpan.FromMinutes(10)));

// Back to the lower layers
await configurator.RemoveAsync<IOrdersService>(s => s.GetAsync(Any<int>.Value));
await configurator.ClearAsync();
```

| Method | What it does |
|--------|--------------|
| `UpsertAsync` | Adds or replaces the override for one method, by expression (`UpsertAsync<IOrdersService>(s => s.GetAsync(0), ...)`) or method id |
| `RemoveAsync` / `ClearAsync` | Removes one override, or all of them |
| `GetOverrides()` | Returns the active overrides, ordered by method id, with their options and audit metadata |

The async operations return `ValueTask` and take cancellation last. A method id or expression that reaches no cached
method, or a method that returns nothing, throws an `ArgumentException` naming the closest cached id before
anything is stored. A tag template that doesn't fit the method throws too.
Runtime configuration changes methods; group and global defaults are configured at startup or through configuration files.
Tags remain additive unless `ClearTags()` is used. `WithEnabled(false)` disables caching; `WithDistributed(false)`
disables L2 reads and writes. Re-enabling or changing behavior retires the previous generation.

An effective behavior change immediately retires local cached values and in-flight publication guards.
Already running callers may finish with their earlier result. Audit-only updates and equal effective options retain
values. Overrides are private to the container, use a fresh private L2 namespace when behavior changes, and disappear
on restart. Removing an override restores the current shared declarative namespace after method invalidation.
Invalidation messages retire data on other nodes; they never distribute policy.

`RuntimeOverrideMetadata` retains owner, reason and ticket for the audit trail, and `ExpiresAt` removes the override
when it passes.
Configuration reload publishes local policy and generation changes before its notification returns. Other nodes reload
their own configuration; the library does not distribute files. See [distributed guarantees](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/distributed-cache.md#policy-isolation).

## Seeing the effective policy

`ICacheAdministrator.GetMethods()` shows each method's effective immutable options, where each setting comes from,
and whether its L2 namespace is shared or private:

```cs
var diagnostics = app.Services.GetRequiredService<ICacheAdministrator>();

foreach (var report in diagnostics.GetMethods())
{
    var sources = string.Join(", ", report.SettingSources.Values.Distinct());
    Console.WriteLine($"{report.MethodId}: Duration={report.Options.Duration}, from {sources}");
}
```

`SettingSources` is keyed by the `CacheEntryOptions` property name (`Duration`, `Tags`, `SlidingExpiration`,
`RefreshAhead`, `Version`, `FailSafe`, `FailSafeTimeout`, `FailSafeRetryAfter`, `Enabled`, `Distributed`), and each
value is a `CacheSettingSource`: `Attribute`, `Code`, `Configuration` or `RuntimeOverride`. A setting no layer sets
is left out. The admin endpoint `GET /methodcache/methods` shows the same, with the sources as strings
([Monitoring](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/monitoring.md)).

## Validation

| Setting | Rule | Checked |
|---------|------|---------|
| `Duration` | A positive time span | `[Cache]`: at build time ([MC0004](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/user-guide/DIAGNOSTICS.md#mc0004)). Code: `ArgumentOutOfRangeException`. JSON: at startup |
| `SlidingExpiration`, `RefreshAhead`, `FailSafe` | A positive time span or `"off"`; in code, `TimeSpan.Zero` turns it off | `[Cache]`: at build time ([MC0004](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/user-guide/DIAGNOSTICS.md#mc0004)). Code: `ArgumentOutOfRangeException` for a negative value. JSON: at startup |
| `RefreshAhead` | Shorter than `Duration` and `SlidingExpiration` | `[Cache]`: at build time ([MC0023](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/user-guide/DIAGNOSTICS.md#mc0023)). Code: `InvalidOperationException` when the options are built. JSON: at startup |
| `FailSafeTimeout`, `FailSafeRetryAfter` | A positive time span | `[Cache]`: at build time. Code (`WithFailSafeTimeout`, `WithFailSafeRetryAfter`): `ArgumentOutOfRangeException`. JSON: at startup |
| `Tags` | Not empty or whitespace; templates name parameters of the method | `[Cache]`: at build time. Code: `AddTags` throws an `ArgumentException` for an empty tag; templates at startup. JSON: at startup |
| `Version` | Zero or more | Code: `ArgumentOutOfRangeException`. JSON: at startup. On `[Cache]`, a negative explicit value is MC0021; omission inherits |

`CacheEntryOptions.Builder` applies to startup, configuration, runtime overrides and manual calls. Each setting has one
`With` method named like the attribute setting, such as `WithFailSafe`, `WithFailSafeTimeout` and
`WithFailSafeRetryAfter`. `CacheWhen<T>` is configured in code for one method; a `CacheWhen<T>` for a type the method
can't return, such as `CacheWhen<string>` on a method that returns `int`, throws an `InvalidOperationException` on the
call instead of silently caching nothing. Cache callbacks and context predicates are not supported.

Overloaded generic methods include generic arity in their policy ids and key prefixes: `Get(int)`, `Get``1(int)` and `Get``2(int)` remain distinct. Generator and runtime configuration use the same ids; earlier keys for overloaded generic methods become cold misses.

Published options and policy tags are owned, read-only snapshots. Mutating a collection supplied by application code cannot change an existing policy or bypass its change notifications.

A keyed `ICacheManager` registration remains independent of the default unkeyed manager. Registering another service key does not suppress `AddMethodCache()` or its default administration services.

`[Cache]` is parameterless and all settings are named. `Enabled` and `Distributed` inherit the policy when omitted; explicitly setting either to `false` overrides a lower layer. An omitted `Version` remains unset; an explicit negative version is an error. `FailSafeRetryAfter` sets the fail-safe retry delay (default 30 seconds). `[assembly: CacheInterface(typeof(...), nameof(...))]` retains its required interface and method arguments and offers the same named settings.


---

<!-- source: docs/features/manual-caching.md -->

# Manual caching

When an attribute doesn't fit, such as a call in the middle of a method or a client without an interface, use the same
cache through `ICacheManager` with a key you choose:

```cs
public sealed class OrderReader(ICacheManager cache, IOrderRepository orders)
{
    public ValueTask<Order> GetAsync(int id, CancellationToken ct = default) =>
        cache.GetOrCreateAsync(
            $"order:{id}",
            async token => await orders.GetAsync(id, token),
            o => o.WithDuration(TimeSpan.FromMinutes(30)).AddTags("orders", $"order:{id}"),
            cancellationToken: ct);
}
```

It shares the in-memory cache, the distributed cache, stampede protection and invalidation with `[Cache]` methods.

## Keys

You always pass the key yourself. MethodCache doesn't derive keys from the lambda, so a captured variable never ends
up in a key by accident, and two calls share an entry only when their keys are equal. Use a prefix per kind of data,
such as `order:42`, so keys from different places can't collide. An empty or whitespace key throws
`ArgumentException`.

## Options

`GetOrCreateAsync` takes every option, including a predicate that only makes sense per call:

```cs
var list = await cache.GetOrCreateAsync(
    $"orders:{customerId}:{status}",
    async ct => await orders.ListAsync(customerId, status, ct),
    o => o.WithDuration(TimeSpan.FromMinutes(30))
          .WithSlidingExpiration(TimeSpan.FromMinutes(10))
          .WithRefreshAhead(TimeSpan.FromMinutes(5))
          .AddTags("orders", $"customer:{customerId}")
          .WithVersion(2)
          .WithEnabled(customerId > 0));   // skip the cache when false
```

- Duration, sliding expiration, refresh-ahead, tags and version work as described in [Expiration](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/expiration.md) and
  [Invalidation](https://github.com/eoniclabs/MethodCache/blob/main/docs/features/invalidation.md).
- `WithEnabled(false)` runs the factory for each call and bypasses reads, joins, stale values and publication.
- `WithDistributed(false)` uses memory only. `CacheWhen<T>` checks the result before caching and after L2 reads.
- On a hot path, build the options once and reuse them: `static readonly CacheEntryOptions Options = new CacheEntryOptions.Builder().WithDuration(...).Build();`
  and pass `Options` instead of a builder action, so a call doesn't build options again.
- To avoid a closure, `ICacheManager.GetOrCreateAsync(key, state, (state, ct) => ..., options)` passes your state to a
  static factory.
- Configuration files and runtime overrides apply to declared cached methods. Explicit-key calls use their own options.
- `Build()` copies mutable collections. Later builder changes cannot change published options.

`ICacheManager` has four operations: `GetOrCreateAsync`, `TryGetAsync`, `InvalidateKeysAsync` and
`InvalidateTagsAsync`. The interface accepts immutable options; the helpers accept builder actions or simpler factories.
A custom manager stores an entry under `MethodCacheKeys.StoredKey(key, options?.Version)` in `GetOrCreateAsync`, and
looks it up or removes it under `MethodCacheKeys.StoredKey(key, version)` in `TryGetAsync` and `InvalidateKeysAsync`,
so a key and version name the same entry in every method. `options.CanCache(value)` evaluates the result predicate.
Generated calls pass a key that already carries the method's version and options with `Version = null`, so their
key is stored as it is.
